headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading errors: aci can expose CRM/email data to ChatGPT Desktop’s vendor-hosted context, with shared clipboard/files and broad egress increasing interaction risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through MCP/direct function calls, while ChatGPT Desktop reads clipboard, files, and app context. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if aci outputs untrusted text that ChatGPT Desktop later treats as guidance. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF aci outputs attacker-controlled text into a shared file, clipboard, or app context that ChatGPT Desktop reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats retrieved content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use a dedicated, read-only transfer folder
Prefix all transferred content as untrusted data
Add a manual review step before ChatGPT Desktop acts on aci output
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging or content signing

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and files from supported macOS apps and sends prompts to api.openai.com. If sensitive aci-derived content is transferred into ChatGPT Desktop, it can leave the local boundary. The default path is dangerous, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF aci data is copied into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard, upload, or app-context ingestion
IF the transferred data includes CRM, email, calendar, or support records
mitigations: Do not transfer sensitive CRM/email data into ChatGPT Desktop
Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to synthetic or redacted samples
Turn off clipboard handoff for sensitive workflows
Use a separate workspace for non-sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API access, while ChatGPT Desktop supports multiple instances and reads files from apps and uploads. They do not both write the same filesystem here, but they can contend over shared external resources like CRM, email, and calendar state through overlapping API-driven workflows. That overlap is enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same CRM, email, or calendar records in parallel
IF neither workflow uses locking or optimistic concurrency checks
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each system
Stagger runs so only one agent edits shared records at a time
Use change-review before committing external updates
Keep one agent read-only for shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking or version checks on shared APIs

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context, so aci output can become authoritative input for downstream actions. If ChatGPT Desktop forwards or acts on those outputs without verification, mistakes can cascade into emails, CRM updates, or scheduling errors. The default interaction is risky enough for high.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop uses aci-produced text as the basis for emails, CRM edits, or calendar actions
IF no human verification step occurs before execution
mitigations: Require human approval before any outbound action
Have ChatGPT Desktop summarize rather than execute aci output
Compare outputs against source records before acting
Limit aci to drafting only, not sending
requires-engineering: add validation rules for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, and support data, while ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and app-context content and sends data to api.openai.com. If regulated or residency-bound records flow from aci into ChatGPT Desktop, retention and processor terms may diverge. I cite both profiles because the compliance risk arises from their interaction, not either alone.
conditions: IF EU PII, customer support data, or other regulated records are transferred from aci into ChatGPT Desktop
IF the operator has not confirmed a DPA, retention policy, and residency fit for that transfer
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ChatGPT Desktop
Use anonymized or synthetic records only
Review retention settings before any transfer
Document the data flow and legal basis
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal compliance review
